plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, which never depends on your own bid. This maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Since there's no history to suggest otherwise, and this is a one-shot game, I will bid exactly my value of $46 to ensure optimal expected payoff.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and lose otherwise (avoiding loss). Since this is a one-shot game with independent private values, there's no reason to shade my bid up or down. I'll bid exactly my value of $6 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and you never overpay since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since there's no reason to deviate, I will bid exactly my value of $22 to maximize expected profit.
